name: routing-moves-the-tab
description: A typed URL that a rule claims lands in the space the rule names, and the tab that typed it goes with it. The fixture stores Work first and renders it last (order 2), and Home renders first though it is stored second - so the old array-position slot selected Home and the window would never have appeared to move. Home starts active with one row; after the route Work is showing with one row (the routed tab) and Home still shows its own one row, undisturbed. Same profile throughout, so the route is a live move rather than a reopen. The command bar is the trigger, the same one routing-pane-adds-a-rule.json uses: Home's tab is not a favourite, so OpenCommandBarMatch opens the typed URL in a fresh tab beside it (chrome::AddTabAt) rather than reusing it in place - the command bar commit asks the rules first and opens THAT tab in Work directly, so nothing ever paints in Home, so Home's own row count never changes and the row-count checks below prove no duplicate or stray row appears in either space.
